newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields end a touch higher, 7/98s rally strongly.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields end a touch higher, 7/98s rally strongly.

text.p: New Zealand two-year bonds stood out at Thursday's close after being squeezed dramatically and rallying 11 basis points to 7.31 percent.
Other bonds finished largely unchanged to a couple of points weaker.
Dealers said the two-year bonds were a real problem, and there were simply not enough in the domestic market.

"There are just about 2.5 billion in the market, of which over two billion are held by offshore people. They're being squeezed by someone and people just aren't able to deliver," one bond dealer said.

He said the last few days had seen a lot of direct buying of New Zealand bonds out of Japan, especially in the 7/98-03/02 part of the curve, where volumes were fairly solid. From the 03/02s out trade had been quiet during the session.
The dealer said the squeeze on the two-year maturities could soon cause problems.

"At the moment, the market is thinking about whether it should be price-making those bonds or not. I think the market is very close to stopping price-making that security, which would be a shame, because it could easily flow onto another security."
He saw the two-years opening on Friday around current levels, but added: "If there is more bidding pressure in there at the start, that could easily be the end of the 98 price-making tomorrow".
Retail sales data, showing a 0.6 percent seasonally adjusted decline in the August month, caused little stir in the market.
NZD VS 3 YR 10 YR * NZD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD

New Zealand 10-year bonds went under Australian bonds on the spread at Thursday's close and also narrowed the spread dramatically against the Aussie three-years, as that market struggled to recover its composure following the Reserve Bank of Australia's quarterly bulletin.
The report expressed concerns over wage growth, casting doubt over the possibility of further monetary policy easing.
The short end of the Australian market had priced in a 50 basis point official rate cut, and selling was aggressive when confirmation of the cut failed to materialise.
